questions.question: What closes an autonomous infrastructure control loop?
options: Receiving a success response from the action API
Verifying that the intended service outcome recovered
Writing an audit log before the action
Running the same action on every resource
questions.explanation: Execution is not success; the controller must observe the user-facing consequence and escalate or compensate when the outcome is unknown.

questions.question: Why should a controller reconcile desired and observed state instead of issuing a one-time script?
options: It removes the need for authority policy
It guarantees the observed state is always current
Repeated idempotent reconciliation can recover from interruption and ongoing drift
It makes external side effects exactly once
questions.explanation: A reconciler keeps comparing durable intent with fresh observations and can retry safely when its operations are idempotent.

questions.question: Which remediation is the strongest candidate for bounded automatic execution?
options: An irreversible regional data migration based on one metric
A fleet-wide patch with no rollback artifact
A destructive storage repair while telemetry is unavailable
A tested replacement of one stateless replica with fresh corroborated evidence
questions.explanation: Automatic authority should begin with well-understood, reversible, narrow actions backed by reliable evidence.

questions.question: What is the main risk of a cooldown shorter than the system's settling time?
options: The controller can react to its own incomplete change and oscillate
The controller loses its audit identity
The telemetry becomes encrypted
The desired state becomes immutable
questions.explanation: Feedback delay can make healthy recovery look ineffective, causing repeated or opposing actions before the first action has settled.

questions.question: Why compare a canary with a stable control when automating rollback?
options: It guarantees the canary has no user traffic
It removes the need for service-level indicators
It helps attribute a regression to the candidate change instead of a shared incident
It makes rollback instantaneous
questions.explanation: Comparable cohorts strengthen causal evidence and reduce false rollback decisions caused by unrelated production changes.

questions.question: What should happen when an ML diagnosis is uncertain or out of distribution?
options: Increase action scope to obtain a clearer signal
Reduce authority, gather evidence, and escalate
Hide the uncertainty from the action policy
Retrain online before preserving the incident
questions.explanation: Prediction is evidence, not authority. Unknown conditions need containment and human review, not broader automatic action.

questions.question: Which pair of controls most directly limits simultaneous remediation conflicts?
options: A larger metric retention window and more dashboards
A higher model confidence score and longer logs
More controllers with the same unrestricted token
Stable action identities and a per-resource conflict lock
questions.explanation: Idempotency and ownership prevent duplicate or competing controllers from mutating the same resource at once.

questions.question: What must an emergency stop path preserve?
options: Independent authority and observability even when the autonomous controller is unhealthy
The same credentials and dependency chain as the controller
Permission to delete the audit history
Automatic restart of every paused remediation
questions.explanation: A kill switch is ineffective if it depends on the same failed control plane or overprivileged identity it must stop.
